Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the revised order form. A couple of quick items we need to lock before routing to legal / PO issuance: 

1) Invoice recipient — can you confirm whether Redwood will invoice OmniHealth US entity (OmniHealth, Inc.) or our EU subsidiary for this contract? Our AP team needs the remit entity to match the PO.

2) Tax withholding — our tax team flagged Sections 4.2/Appendix B. Does Redwood expect OmniHealth to gross up for any withholding taxes or provide tax evidence to avoid withholding?

3) Net terms — procurement prefers Net30 but finance typically requires Net45 for new vendors. Can Redwood accept Net30 with standard SLAs? If not, please confirm Net45 and we’ll escalate.

4) Can we get a marked-up order form (tracked redlines)? We will push PO once the invoice path and tax responsibility are clear.

Subject: Re: OMH order form - invoice routing + tax questions

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and next steps below.

- Invoice recipient: Redwood prefers to invoice OmniHealth, Inc. (US) for this engagement to avoid cross-border VAT handling on our side. If you must have the EU entity as payer, we can support that but will need to confirm tax residency and entity details (Entity name, tax id, address).
- Tax withholding: Redwood does not expect customers to gross up by default. If OmniHealth is subject to withholding under local law, customer is responsible unless a tax certificate (or treaty claim) is provided that eliminates withholding. We can accept a certificate from your tax team as evidence to waive withholding.
- Net terms: Our commercial team prefers Net45 for new accounts. Ben — can finance support Net30 with an early-pay discount or other trade?

Next steps I propose:
1) I will attach a tracked-redline of the order form with the invoice recipient clause clarified and a short appendix we can sign to capture the entity to invoice. (See attached redlines_OMH_orderform.docx)
2) Ben / Kimberly — can you provide (a) confirmation on Net terms and (b) any standard language around tax evidence?
3) Alex — if you can confirm the preferred remit entity and send the PO template we’ll align the doc then route to legal for a quick sign-off.

I’ve attached: OMH_OrderForm_v3.pdf and a draft redline.

Best,

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 11:04 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and next steps below.

Finance position (summary):
- Net terms: Standard onboarding cadence is Net45. We can accept Net30 only with one of the following: (i) a 2% 10-day early-payment discount, or (ii) a payment guarantee (PO + 30-day auto-approve) for the first invoice. We prefer option (i) if procurement can accept it.
- Invoice remit entity: We can invoice OmniHealth, Inc. (US) as Naomi suggested. If you require an EU entity invoice, we need the EU entity’s VAT registration and a confirmation email copied to accounting@redwood.com.
- Withholding/taxes: Customer is responsible for withholding where applicable. To avoid withholding, we require either (a) a local tax residency certificate or (b) a signed treaty benefit/withholding exemption form. If OmniHealth provides the tax cert (scanned PDF), accounting will ingest and flag for future invoices.

I’ve attached the redlined order form with a short commercial appendix showing the Net30 w/2%/10 option and an invoice entity table (redlines_OMH_orderform.docx). Also attached our tax evidence checklist (OMH_Tax_Certificate.pdf).

If that meets your team’s needs we can finalize and send a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
